answer: Divergent challenge ladders. Each identity gets a saffron-coded seed that mutates on every signed action, and the agent must publish the next link before its counterpart can act. A clone copying the transcript produces a matching spiral of hashes but cannot answer the fresh challenge without the private state, so duplication stalls at the first divergence. The voyage through the ladder costs one unique proof-of-work step per identity per epoch, pricing each fake identity at real compute that scales linearly with the number of clones.
